pr.title: Avoid cloning jump threading state when possible
pr.description:
The current implementation of jump threading passes most of its time cloning its state. This PR attempts to avoid such clones by special-casing the last predecessor when recursing through a terminator.

This is not optimal, but a first step while I refactor the state data structure to be sparse.

The two other commits are drive-by.
Fixes https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/issues/116721

pr.author: cjgillot

processing.reason: The PR's JumpThreading change is a semantics-preserving clone-avoidance refactor, not a wrong value transformation. It clones the accumulated ConditionSet for every non-last predecessor and moves it only for the last predecessor, after all clone-taking paths; the callee still obtains one independent State per recursion and mutates only its per-call local via flood_with. The real bug fix in this PR is the rustc_mir_dataflow/value_analysis slice-scalar assert removal for #116721, whose regression test is build-pass/--emit=mir only (and the deleted test was known-bug), so no runtime original-vs-transformed value divergence is justified. Encoding a share/mutate-one-state bug would be a fabricated unrelated rewrite, not the historical incorrect transformation. Frozen analysis's own testStrategy confirms no runtime behavior difference should be claimed.

analysis.originalLogic: In `find_opportunity`, the pre-PR traversal handled multiple predecessors with a plain loop: `for &pred in predecessors { self.recurse_through_terminator(pred, &state, &cost, depth); }`, and `recurse_through_terminator` accepted `state: &State<ConditionSet<'a>>` and did `let mut state = state.clone();` only after deciding it could recurse. The single/other arm likewise passed `&state`. Thus every traversed predecessor took a clone, even the last one whose state could be consumed, and the clone was made before the callee knew whether it needed the state.
analysis.incorrectTransformation: Historically, the traversal eagerly cloned the accumulated condition state for every predecessor before recursing. The PR changes the callee to accept `impl FnOnce() -> State<ConditionSet<'a>>`, passes `|| state.clone()` for all non-last predecessors, and passes `|| state` for `last_pred`, so the final traversal moves the state instead of cloning it. There is no source-backed claim that the old behavior changed program semantics; it was the performance-incorrect transformation for this pass. The correctness-sensitive alternative to avoid is sharing, consuming, or mutating one state across multiple predecessor traversals, since the local state is later modified by `state.flood_with(...)`.
analysis.inputDomain: MIR bodies containing switch terminators whose discriminant is mapped by value analysis, with backward predecessor walks reaching join blocks that have multiple predecessors. The traversal excludes cleanup blocks and loop headers. Relevant paths include a single-predecessor switch continuation, where the new closure can move `state`, and a multiple-predecessor join, where all but the last predecessor must receive clones.
analysis.summary: JumpThreading avoids eager state cloning during backward predecessor traversal by passing a lazy state-producing closure and moving the state only for the last predecessor. The invariant is that every predecessor recursion must receive an independent state unless it is the one path allowed to consume the original state, and the move must occur after the clone-taking paths.
analysis.trigger: A jump-threading backward walk reaches a block with multiple predecessors, especially after a switch, so the same accumulated `ConditionSet` state would otherwise be cloned once per predecessor. The new single-predecessor arm and the final predecessor in the multi-predecessor arm can move the state instead of cloning it.
preconditions: The pass has a switch terminator with a discriminant place that value analysis can map.
A predecessor traversal reaches a block with one or more predecessors.
The original `state` remains unmodified while earlier predecessors receive clones.
`recurse_through_terminator` can early-return before invoking the state closure, so cloning must remain lazy.
Only the last predecessor may consume the original state.
pitfalls: Do not move or share one state across multiple predecessor recursions; each branch must observe the same pre-flood conditions.
The local state is mutated after `state()` via `flood_with`, so a state consumed by one branch cannot safely be reused by a sibling branch.
The move for the last predecessor is only safe after all other predecessors have taken clones.
The empty-predecessor case must remain a no-op; the slice pattern `&[ref predecessors @ .., last_pred]` handles that, unlike assuming a last element exists.
This is a compile-time optimization with no expected runtime-output change; do not derive semantic test differences from it.
analysis.testStrategy: Exercise the pass on MIR-level CFGs with a switch on a known discriminant followed by a join block with multiple predecessors, and include a single-predecessor switch path to hit the move branch. Verify the same threading opportunities/MIR are produced and that compilation still succeeds; the supplied PR adds no dedicated clone-avoidance regression test, so existing MIR tests and build-pass coverage are the available guard. Do not claim runtime behavioral differences.
